title: Wendell and the Wardrobe
premise: Edmund Okafor has spent nineteen years inspecting bridges while his marriage quietly corrodes, measuring everything but never intervening. At his mother-in-law's funeral, a stranger named Wendell addresses the family by 'Adeyemi'—a name his wife Ruth buried along with her first identity, a name that belongs to a man Wendell claims was wronged. As the family house sale looms, Edmund and Ruth must return to the coastal town where Ruth's brother disappeared decades ago and where her silence purchased their safety. Edmund, the man of measurement, must finally choose loyalty to truth over loyalty to the life he built on Ruth's lie, exposing her family at the cost of their marriage—only to find that confession, not concealment, is what lets them finally own their days.
about_author: Ivo Oyelaran is a former structural engineer who left the profession after a decade of inspecting bridges in three countries, and now writes fiction about the weight-bearing points of human lives. He lives between Lagos and Liverpool, where he still cannot walk across a bridge without touching the railing.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. We meet Edmund mid-inspection on a decaying viaduct, a man fluent in tolerances and gaps who cannot name the widening gap in his own marriage. At home, Ruth moves through rooms like a guest. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the sense that something structural has already failed, unnoticed, beneath the surface.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew the Name
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ruth's alternating POV. At Ruth's mother's funeral, an old man in a grey suit calls Ruth 'Adaeze' and the family 'Adeyemi.' Ruth goes white; her brother Chidi's name is spoken for the first time in thirty years. Emotional beat: rupture—the past arriving uninvited at the most public moment of grief.

chapters.title: What the Photograph Held
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Alone, Ruth studies the photograph: Chidi, herself, and a courthouse steps she recognizes instantly. She burns nothing and tells Edmund nothing. Flashback fragments of the town of Ilaro and the night in 1989. Emotional beat: guilt calcifying into habit—Ruth choosing the familiar silence one more time.

chapters.title: Load-Bearing
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finds the photograph while boxing up the house for sale. He confronts Ruth gently; she deflects with logistics—escrow, movers, the estate lawyer. Their daughter Tami arrives, sensing the fault line. Emotional beat: the marriage as a bridge under unreported load, inspectors on both sides certifying it safe.

chapters.title: Wendell
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund tracks Wendell to a boarding house near the docks. Wendell, once Chidi's friend and the family's driver, reveals fragments: Chidi didn't run away; he was disappeared after witnessing something involving Ruth and her mother's silence, a death ruled accidental. Emotional beat: Edmund's loyalty to Ruth cracking against his hunger for truth.

chapters.title: The House Sale
chapters.summary: Tami's POV. Tami, home to sign paperwork, discovers her parents sleeping in separate rooms and the photograph hidden in Grandma's Bible. She confronts Edmund, who tells her almost everything. Emotional beat: the daughter as reluctant inspector of her parents' structure, furious that truth was managed like a liability.

chapters.title: Ilaro, 1989
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV, a long flashback chapter. The full night revealed: Chidi saw their mother's business partner kill a clerk and pin it on an innocent man; the partner, now a judge, threatened the family; sixteen-year-old Ruth chose silence to survive, and her mother chose it to protect her. Emotional beat: compassion for the girl who had no good options.

chapters.title: Before Escrow Closes
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ruth's alternating POV. With five days before closing, Edmund tells Ruth they must go to Ilaro—not to expose her, but because he cannot live as a tenant of her silence any longer. Ruth's rage and terror; then, at midnight, she wakes him: 'Book the tickets.' Emotional beat: love against duty—Ruth choosing truth at the possible cost of everything.

chapters.title: The Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: Edmund, Ruth, and Tami's rotating POV. In Ilaro, Wendell leads them to the judge—now dying, still powerful. Ruth testifies to a retired magistrate and a journalist, naming the partner and the innocent man who died in prison. The judge's men threaten them; Wendell stands in the doorway. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, costly and imperfect, but spoken.

chapters.title: Owner, Not Tenant
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue-like. Months later: the case reopened, the house sale cancelled, the family staying in a smaller rented flat that Ruth chose herself. Edmund and Ruth walk a new bridge he helped certify; she touches the railing the way he does. Emotional beat: resolution—truth did not save them cheaply, but it made the marriage theirs.
